tweets: 1/8 A controlled AI demo can be impressive. Enterprise readiness is a different test: can the system keep working when data, permissions, exceptions, tools, and accountability become real?

2/8 A demo may read one request and return a quote. In production, the same task must verify the customer, product, inventory, price conditions, access rights, missing data, conflicts, and escalation paths.

3/8 RAND interviewed 65 experienced AI engineers and researchers across 50+ organizations. Reported failure drivers included unclear problems and metrics, weak data, infrastructure gaps, and capability mismatch. https://www.rand.org/pubs/research_reports/RRA2680-1.html

4/8 MIT CISR also frames scale as more than technology: strategy, systems, people and team collaboration, and governance must mature together. https://cisr.mit.edu/publication/2025_0801_EnterpriseAIMaturityUpdate_WoernerSebastianWeillKaganer
5/8 Five practical checks: Is the business problem real? Is enterprise knowledge trusted and current? Are tool permissions explicit? Are exceptions handled? Is the task measurable and traceable?

6/8 NIST treats governance, context mapping, measurement, and management as lifecycle concerns—not a final compliance step. https://www.nist.gov/publications/artificial-intelligence-risk-management-framework-generative-artificial-intelligence

7/8 JovaAI treats professional agents as a governed collaboration unit. Each role needs a task, tools, limits, escalation conditions, and a clear handoff. JovaOS carries and governs those relationships.
8/8 Do not judge enterprise AI only by its best demo moment. Ask whether it can finish a real task repeatedly while keeping the process visible, the boundaries controllable, and accountability clear.
